newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zacatecas state sees higher metals output. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zacatecas state sees higher metals output. [CORRECTED]

text.p: Mexico's Zacatecas state expects to produce 1,014 tonnes (corrects from 1,104) of silver in 1996, up from 940 tonnes last year, said Felipe Martinez, the state mining director.
"Silver production is estimated at 1,014 tonnes" for 1996, Martinez told Reuters in a telephone inteview.
The north-central state also is expecting to produce 745 kg of gold, 22,000 tonnes of copper, 123,000 tonnes of zinc and 46,000 tonnes of lead in 1996, Martinez said.
Those numbers are higher for all but lead production.
In 1995, Zacatecas produced 631.6 kg of gold, 17,095 tonnes of copper, 99,515 tonnes of zinc, and 49,258 tonnes of lead, Mrtinez said.
Martinez said Zacatecas would continue to lead all Mexican states in production of silver, place second in copper and zinc and sixth in gold at the end of 1996.
